1: Depth-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Reconstruction of Dense Brain MRI Volumes from Sparse Slices
2: Problem: sparse axial sampling leaves unobserved planes and can obscure structures during volume resampling. Solution: A computer-implemented research system reconstructs missing axial brain MRI slices from sparse acquired slices. A shared residual convolutional encoder processes the bounding slices. Three-coordinate Fourier embeddings encode normalized depth, relative position and slice gap. Spatial context and cross-attention tokens condition a latent denoising U-Net; DDIM sampling and a pretrained VAE decoder generate missing slices. Assembly optionally smooths along depth and restores acquired slices exactly. The demonstrated scope is retrospective FLAIR MRI reconstruction; scanner acquisition acceleration and diagnostic efficacy are proposed applications requiring separate validation.
3: Sparse-to-dense MRI; missing-slice synthesis; through-plane super-resolution; conditional latent diffusion; neighboring-slice conditioning; Fourier depth embedding; hybrid spatial/cross-attention conditioning; DDIM; acquired-slice preservation; volume interpolation; intensity calibration.
4: Present methods include nearest/linear/cubic interpolation, learned slice synthesis, latent diffusion (R1/R2), and approaches addressing inter-slice stochasticity (R3). Commercial AI reconstruction such as Deep Resolve (R8) also exists. Classical interpolation is inexpensive but limited by sampled anatomy; learned priors can generate plausible unsupported detail. The implemented system has no k-space/sinogram measurement model, explicit 3D consistency loss, calibrated uncertainty or clinical validation.
5: Established latent diffusion and cross-attention: R1. Sparse cardiac MRI latent reconstruction: CaLID, R2, a close conceptual overlap. Inter-slice noise consistency: ISCS, R3. Missing-slice binary interpolation: US11410271B2, R4. Multi-slice 2D diffusion/3D conversion patent lead: R5 (full text unavailable). See attached source register and PRIOR_ART.md. No head-to-head evaluation against these learned systems was performed.
6: A practical implementation gap is addressed: reproducible MRI slice reconstruction on a local 8 GB GPU with acquired-only calibration and explicit data preservation. A major gap in prior art has not been established; CaLID substantially overlaps sparse MRI latent interpolation. The specific combined conditioning design needs further full-text comparison and an inventor-confirmed disclosure timeline.

8: Input: a registered depth-first stack (D,C,H,W) and unique acquired depth indices including both boundaries. Validate channels, dimensions, finite values and checkpoints. 9: Candidate distinguishing combination: acquired-only intensity calibration plus weight-tied bounding-slice encoding, explicit global-depth/relative-offset/gap embeddings, hybrid spatial/token conditioning and exact acquired-slice restoration. These elements are implemented. Individual latent diffusion, cross-attention and slice interpolation concepts are already known (R1-R4). Novelty and inventive step remain unestablished; broad superiority or a first-in-field claim would exceed the evidence.

Working example: D=155, C=1, H=W=240. At stride 8, acquired indices include 0,8,...,152,154 (21 acquired and 134 missing); at stride 16 they include 0,16,...,144,154 (11 acquired and 144 missing). A target at z=12 bounded by z=8 and z=16 has alpha=0.5, depth=12/154 and normalized gap=0.5. Context is computed only from those acquired slices. The trained VAE maps a 240x240 image to four 30x30 latent channels: 8x spatial downsampling per axis and 16x scalar-element reduction for FLAIR. Code path and results are supplied in sections 15-17.

Historical evidence retained separately: ten-volume evaluation recorded diffusion PSNR_missing 27.785 dB at stride 8 and 25.260 dB at stride 16; these earlier results used different preprocessing and must not be pooled with the corrected experiment. Best stored VAE checkpoint is epoch 13, validation loss 0.0891816; diffusion checkpoint is epoch 48, noise loss 0.1177198. Those losses are not image-fidelity metrics.
Coordinates: alpha=(z-z_prev)/(z_next-z_prev), depth=z/(D-1), gap=(z_next-z_prev)/16. Normalization: I_norm=2*(clip(I,vmin,vmax)-vmin)/(vmax-vmin+epsilon)-1, with background mapped to -1 and epsilon=1e-7. Clean latent: z0=0.18215*(mu+sigma*epsilon). Forward diffusion: z_t=sqrt(alpha_bar_t)*z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon. Noise objective: E[||epsilon-epsilon_theta(z_t,t,context)||^2]. Deterministic DDIM: predicted z0=(z_t-sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon_theta)/sqrt(alpha_bar_t); z_prev=sqrt(alpha_bar_prev)*predicted z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_prev)*epsilon_theta. VAE objective: L1+0.5*MSE+1e-5*KL+0.1*spatial-gradient L1. Reconstruction MSE=mean((prediction-target)^2); MAE=mean(abs(prediction-target)); PSNR=10*log10(4/MSE) for [-1,1], capped at 100 dB for near-perfect matches. SSIM uses an 11x11 Gaussian window (sigma 1.5), constants (0.01*2)^2 and (0.03*2)^2, averaged over 2D slices/channels.
16: Python 3.10; measured environment PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128 on NVIDIA RTX 5060 Laptop GPU (approximately 8 GB VRAM). From the project directory, use the approved interpreter D:\Kaggle competetion\torch_env\Scripts\python.exe. Example commands: -m pytest tests -q; scripts/reconstruct_volume.py --vol_id 14 --stride 8 --seed 42 --steps 25; scripts/evaluate_all.py --vols 10 --strides 8 16; scripts/finetune_diffusion.py --init-checkpoint experiments/checkpoints/diffusion/best_model.pt --strides 4 8 16 --lr 2e-5 --time-limit-minutes 70 --output-dir experiments/review/new_run. scripts/review_experiment.py reproduces the complete bounded protocol. Resume uses an explicit --resume checkpoint. Source implements epsilon prediction and DDIM; DDPM inference and arbitrary encoder backbones are not implemented.
17: Local data: 57,195 HDF5 slice files representing 369 volume IDs, each 155 axial planes at 240x240. Each image has four stored channels; current code assumes FLAIR/T1/T1ce/T2 ordering, which requires original HDF5 converter provenance confirmation. Three uint8 mask channels exist; sampled channels are mutually exclusive, so WT/TC/ET semantics are not assumed. Original BraTS is multi-institutional brain-tumor MRI with expert annotations (R6). Patient-volume split uses seed 42: 258 train, 55 validation, 56 test. These are internal partitions of the local training collection, not official challenge test data. Diffusion trains only on missing target planes. Fine-tuning uses equal-probability strides 4/8/16 and acquired-only intensity statistics; VAE stays frozen and encoder/U-Net receive MSE noise-prediction updates with AdamW and gradient clipping. Five fixed validation volumes select settings; ten held-out volumes provide final comparisons. No external data or third-party clinical study is used. Fine-tuning completed 3000 training iterations (24000 sampled slice examples with replacement) in 18.49 minutes, stopping at the configured step cap within the 70-minute limit. The candidate did not satisfy the validation improvement criterion, so the corrected original checkpoint remains selected.
